title: Who is worthier than you
hook: tradition says the nine-year-old told his father no one was worthier to answer the Kashmiris' plea
tomorrow: a court of poets at Anandpur

segments.voice: Yesterday, a child at Patna Sahib: armies of children, archery by the Ganges, chickpeas in Rani Maini's lap. Your line was the boy by the river.

Anandpur, 1675, the scene from day seventy-seven. The pandits of Kashmir have told their story. The Guru sits in silence, heavy with it. The boy from Patna, about nine now and living with his father at last, walks in, sees his father's face, and asks what's wrong. Sometimes a child says the thing the adults have been circling for hours. The family is arguing about moving grandma in, and a seven-year-old says, well, she's lonely, isn't she? The room goes quiet. Everyone knew. Nobody had said it.
screen: `BACK TO ANANDPUR, 1675.` → `WHAT'S WRONG, FATHER?` → `A CHILD SAYS WHAT EVERYONE KNOWS.`

segments.voice: Here is the exchange as Sikh tradition tells it. Guru Tegh Bahadur explains, simply, what the pandits have come for: they're being forced to give up their faith, and nobody can protect them. Then he says the hard part out loud. It would take the sacrifice of a great and holy person to stop this. The boy thinks about it, the way children do, completely seriously. And he answers: who could be worthier than you, father? A handful of words from a nine-year-old. Tradition is clear that the boy understood what he was saying. He was offering his father. And his father heard it not as a child's mistake, but as an answer. Tradition says the Guru was glad, because he saw that his son was ready to lead. He told the pandits to go to the authorities and say: if Guru Tegh Bahadur accepts conversion, we all will. Then he named Gobind Rai as the next Guru and set out for Delhi, knowing where the road went. You already know the rest. What Sikhs take from this moment is the courage of the boy: a child of nine gave up his father for people who weren't even his community, because it was right. That boy became the tenth Guru. The line people carry from it is simpler: when something needs doing, and you're wondering who should do it, sometimes the honest answer is: who better than you?
screen: `NOBODY CAN PROTECT THEM.` · `IT WOULD TAKE A GREAT SACRIFICE.` · `WHO IS WORTHIER THAN YOU?` · `A NINE-YEAR-OLD NAMED GURU.` · then, large: `WHO BETTER THAN YOU.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone at the edge of something hard: a surgery, a hard conversation, a new job, a decision they're afraid of. Picture their face, and picture yourself saying to them, simply and warmly: you can do this. Who better than you?
Gobind Rai. The tenth Guru's name as a boy, who at nine years old told his father there is no one worthier than you.
Your line: who better than you. A few words from a child, and his father heard an answer. See you tomorrow.
